Answer: C
Reason: The images show multiple variable-sized cystic lesions in the fetal lung (Figure 1) with blood flow present on color Doppler (Figure 2), which is characteristic of Congenital Cystic Adenomatoid Malformation (CCAM). While the question stem specifies Type II (which typically has microcysts and poor prognosis), the visual evidence of macrocysts and vascularity aligns best with Option C's description of "variable-sized cystic lesions" and "potential postnatal complications," distinguishing it from the incorrect descriptions of avascular lesions or single cysts in other options. Note: CCAM type I is macrocystic, type II is microcystic; the image shows a mix, but option C is the most descriptive of the visible pathology among the choices provided that fits a CCAM diagnosis requiring management consideration.
